Hillview Business Park
Location (city/township; county): Arden Hills; RamseyProcess: VarianceStep: Variance denied
Variance description: Maplewood Development and Construction, Inc. (“Maplewood Development” or “Proposer”), seeks to construct a business park, the Hillview Business Park (the “Project”).  The Project is located in the City of Arden Hills on a 62-acre site in Sections 9-10, Township 30N, Range 23W.  The Project is located on the Twin Cities Army Ammunition Plant (“TCAAP”) property.  The City of Arden Hills is preparing an Environmental Impact Statement (EIS) on the Project under rules adopted by the Minnesota Environmental Quality Board (“EQB”).  Maplewood Development is seeking a variance from an EQB rule that prohibits construction activities before the EIS is complete so that it can proceed with demolition of abandoned buildings on the site. Maplewood Development states that demolition is necessary to reduce trespassing, vandalism, and fires in the abandoned buildings while Arden Hills completes the EIS.  The EQB rules allow a variance to be granted to avoid a serious threat to public health or safety.  
At the October 21, 2026 Board meeting, the EQB voted to deny the variance application.

Hwy 252/I-94 Project
Location (city/township; county): Brooklyn Park, Brooklyn Center, Minneapolis; HennepinProcess: EISStep: Draft EISEnd of comment period: December 22, 2026
Project description: The Hwy 252/I-94 Project is located in Hennepin County and includes approximately 12 miles of Hwy 252 and I-94 in the cities of Brooklyn Park, Brooklyn Center, and Minneapolis. Hwy 252 is a principal arterial expressway connecting the northwestern Twin Cities metropolitan area to Minneapolis, while I-94 is a major regional freeway corridor. Currently, people using Hwy 252 and I-94 experience a high number of crashes, traffic congestion, and barriers to walking and biking across the corridor. The purpose of the project is to improve the safe and reliable movement of people and goods across multiple modes on and across Hwy 252 and I-94 between Hwy 610 in Brooklyn Park and North 4th Street in Minneapolis.
The Minnesota Department of Transportation (MnDOT), in cooperation with the Federal Highway Administration (FHWA), has prepared both a Federal Draft Environmental Impact Statement (EIS) and a State Draft EIS for the Highway 252/I-94 Project between Highway 610 in Brooklyn Park and North 4th Street in Minneapolis.
The State Draft EIS has been prepared in accordance with the Minnesota Environmental Policy Act (MEPA) and includes a chapter addressing state-specific environmental review requirements. The Federal Draft EIS has been prepared pursuant to the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA). The two documents are otherwise substantially similar and evaluate the same project alternatives, impacts, mitigation measures, and Preferred Alternative.
The public is invited to review the Draft EIS documents and provide comments during the 60-day comment period, between October 23, 2026 and December 22, 2026.
Additional information, public hearing details, and access to the State Draft EIS is available at MnDOT's project page.

Announcements
EIS Scoping Rule – public comment opportunity
The EQB has issued a Notice of Submission of Exempt Rules Proposed for Adoption Without a Public Hearing; Revisor's ID R-04978, CAH Docket Number 21-9008-41465, for the EIS scoping rule amendments. Submit comments to the Court of Administrative Hearings via its eComments website or to 600 North Robert Street, P.O. Box 64620, St. Paul, Minnesota 55164-64620. You can submit your questions, comments, and feedback on the proposed rule to the administrative law judge assigned to this rulemaking. 
Comment period closes Tuesday, March 17, 2026, at 4:30 p.m.
For more information on the rule and or the rulemaking process, please visit the EQB Rules and regulations webpage.
 
Environmental Review Implementation Subcommittee meeting
Wednesday, March 18, 1 – 4 p.m.Join us in person or virtually for the March 2026 Environmental Review Implementation Subcommittee (ERIS) meeting. At this meeting, ERIS will vote to elect a Chair and Vice Chair. The subcommittee will also hear about the 2025 Environmental Review Performance Report, get a final update on the Minnesota Environmental Review Climate Calculator, and an update on gas production rulemaking. 
More information about the meeting, including the meeting packet and virtual meeting information, can be found on the ERIS meeting webpage.
 
Environmental Review 101: Minnesota Conservation Explorer & Natural Heritage Review
Join EQB staff and Jim Drake, Natural Heritage Review Specialist at the Department of Natural Resources (DNR) for a webinar on using the Minnesota Conservation Explorer (MCE) to address EAW Question 14. This session will cover the data available in the MCE, its use in conservation planning and environmental review, and step-by-step guidance for requesting natural heritage review documentation.
Date: Tuesday, March 31Time: 10:00-11:00 a.m.Register on Teams
After registering, you will receive a confirmation email containing information about joining the meeting.

Notice of Intent to Adopt Expedited Permanent Rules Without a Public Hearing
Proposed Amendments to Rules Governing Environmental Review and Energy Infrastructure, Minnesota Rules, Chapter 4410.
The Environmental Quality Board (EQB) published a notice in the October, 6 2025, Minnesota State Register, and is requesting comment on the proposed amendments to the rules related to environmental review of energy projects. Comments are due by 4:30 pm on November 14, 2025. The notice is available on the EQB rulemaking webpage.
The proposed rule amendments address legislative changes. They update the environmental review process for large energy infrastructure facility projects, make necessary changes to Responsible Governmental Unit (RGU) assignments, publishing requirements, definitions, and mandatory category rules authorized under Minnesota Rules, ch. 4410. The EQB must use the expedited rulemaking process authorized under Minnesota Statutes, 116D.04, subd. 5a., to reflect the changes made in Minn. Law 2024, Ch. 126, Art. 7 and Art. 9, Sec. 2 and 17.

Project description: Holcim‐MWR, Inc. proposes to expand their existing limestone quarry, known as the Larson Quarry, to the east onto an adjacent 148‐acre property that they own located east of County Road 75. Location (city/township; county): Oakdale; WashingtonProcess: EAWStep: EIS need decision
Responsible governmental unit decision: Negative (no EIS ordered)Responsible governmental unit record of decision date: July 18, 2025
Project description: 3M Chemical Operations is proposing a project to collect surface water upstream of the Abresch Disposal Site, to reduce polyfluoroalkyl substances in stormwater discharge from the site. The Abresch Site is the largest of three former disposal sites that comprise the Oakdale Disposal Site, a state and federal superfund site. The project is proposed to further reduce PFAS impacts to stormwater discharge from the site. The proposed project would collect surface water upstream of the site and divert it in a 0.74-mile-long surface water conveyance pipe to a three-acre flood retention basin, where water would then be re-introduced into the natural flow of the watershed. The conveyance pipe would bypass the Abresch Disposal Site, thus bypassing PFAS detected within the site. This would reduce the discharge of PFAS in surface water and improve downstream surface water quality in the Twin Cities east metropolitan area.3M Oakdale Surface Water Diversion Project project link provided by RGU
